results.title: Cutting the sampling tail does not help at temperature 1
results.what: Min-p and top-p truncation at temperature 1.0 scored 404 to 412 of 500 for the cued base, within noise of untruncated sampling (410). RL moved by +0.6 points.
results.why: Truncating the tail brings repetition loops back: loops went from 0 to 34 at min-p 0.1, and length-cap hits from 27 to 58.
results.caveat: One sample per setting. Two samples of one setting disagree on 76 to 85 problems, so gains under about 3.5 points cannot be seen.

results.title: Forcing long answers to commit loses hard problems
results.what: Cutting the cued base's answers at 8,000 tokens and forcing a final boxed answer scored 152 of 328 harder problems, against 164 when left to run, while using about a third fewer tokens.
results.why: Answers that hit the length cap are failures to solve: a forced answer is right on at most 2 of the 77 that hit it, and a hand read found most forced answers were guesses.
